evidence.description: Every remaining reference to REQ-204/PROP-204a in behavioral-spec.md is explicitly meta/historical (revision note, Scope-of-increment note, purity-boundary-table 'OUT OF SCOPE' row, REQ-203's scope-boundary edge case and acceptance-criterion bullet). None of these references creates or implies an active, binding obligation on REQ-204's content. No dangling acceptance criterion anywhere in the file assumes REQ-204 still exists as live scope.

Every remaining reference to REQ-204/PROP-204a in verification-architecture.md (revision note, purity-boundary-map 'OUT OF SCOPE' row, PROP-203b's Tool/Method scope note, Gate item (4)'s bracketed scope note) is likewise explicitly historical/meta, consistently instructing a Phase 3 adversary NOT to check for or fail on prompt.mjs's pre-existing content. No PROP-204a-shaped obligation is smuggled back in under a different name.

SPEC.md's only REQ-204 mention is a dated ('2026-07-07') historical note describing the backlog split and pointing to FIND-401.json -- consistent with the spec-side scope note, not a duplicate/conflicting normative requirement.

Read the actual current code the REQ-201/202/203 wiring will sit on top of: activeSkillSlots/skillCatalog are already computed entirely inside index.mjs from registry.json and passed into assembleContext/buildSystemPrompt as plain arguments; buildSystemPrompt already accepts an externally-supplied activeSkillSlots list, and getToolDefinitions already appends the sleep tool unconditionally regardless of the slots argument. This confirms, against real code (not just the spec's own claim), that filterCatalog + its index.mjs wiring can narrow the live-slot list WITHOUT ever touching prompt.mjs's source text -- so REQ-203/PROP-203b's 'new code only, not an audit of prompt.mjs's pre-existing content' scoping is achievable as stated and does not covertly require re-engaging with the retired REQ-204 content.

FIND-001 (BOOTSTRAP_RESERVE_USDC default), FIND-002 (alwaysAvailable override), FIND-003 (hl_trade close-deadlock carve-out), FIND-004 (isLockStale extraction made BINDING), FIND-005 (PROP-203b's prior false 'you decide' baseline claim -- now removed entirely, not just narrowed), FIND-006 (Phase-3-must-independently-reattack language), FIND-101 (17-slot registry classification table, BINDING), and FIND-102 (hasOpenRiskPositionOf split into yield/hl_trade mechanisms with fail-open default) all remain intact, unweakened, and unaffected by the REQ-204 scope cut in the current revision of both spec files.

FIND-201/FIND-301/FIND-401/FIND-402/FIND-403 (all specific to REQ-204/PROP-204a/PROP-203b's now-retired whole-file audit) are correctly rendered moot, not silently 'fixed' -- the mechanism they attacked (a closed enumeration of prompt.mjs steering phrases/sections) no longer exists in this increment's scope at all, which is the documented, Dais-approved resolution path (backlog, not further patching).
